claim_text: Paré et al observed that Clinic A online/self-booked appointments had a missed-appointment rate averaging 2.1%, versus 7.6% for appointments made traditionally/offline.
quote: The percentage of online appointments that were missed varied from 0.6% to 4.3%, averaging 2.1%.
notes: Primary mixed-methods e-booking study; observational, not randomized.

claim_text: The same Paré Clinic A comparison found traditional/offline missed appointments averaged 7.6%.
quote: Considering appointments made in the traditional manner, missed appointments represented 4.1% to 12.6% of the total and averaged 7.6%.
notes: Same source as E001; same independence group.

claim_text: The 2017 systematic review selected 36 articles covering 21 web-based appointment systems.
quote: A total of 36 articles discussing 21 Web-based appointment systems were selected for this review.

claim_text: The systematic review warns that web-based appointment studies could not be directly compared because their systems differed.
quote: As a result, these studies cannot be directly compared.
notes: Decision-support claim: no pooled universal causal effect. Corroborated by source heterogeneity and confounder branches.

claim_text: Cao et al reported 14.4% non-attendance among users of a Chinese hospital web-based appointment system, while the paper mainly showed wait-time and satisfaction benefits rather than a clean no-show comparator.
quote: The overall proportion of non-attendance was 14.4% for those using the web-based appointment system
notes: Primary web appointment system study; comparator was queuing for satisfaction/waiting, not no-show.

claim_text: In an outpatient ophthalmology clinic, no-show rate increased as appointment lead time increased; lead time is a major confounder for self-scheduling effects.
quote: The no-show rate increased, and the likelihood an appointment would be kept decreased as the time in advance an appointment was scheduled increased.

claim_text: Kheirkhah et al found mean no-show rate of 18.8% and only a modest reminder-associated reduction from 16.3% to 15.8%.
quote: The no-show rate remained at a high level despite its reduction by a centralized phone reminder (from 16.3 % down to 15.8 %).
notes: Large VA retrospective cohort; reminder evidence, not self-scheduling.

claim_text: Hallsworth et al showed SMS wording can reduce missed appointments from 11.1% to 8.4%, illustrating that reminder design can be mistaken for a scheduling-channel effect.
quote: a message including the cost of a missed appointment to the health system produced a DNA rate of 8.4%, compared to 11.1% for the existing message
